request.spec: Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.

agent.result_text:
Done. The full build passes.

## Summary

The `GET /api/owners/{id}` endpoint returns an `OwnerDto` generated from `openapi.yml` and populated via MapStruct's `OwnerMapper`. I added the `initials` field following the same pattern as the existing computed `displayName`:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `initials` property to the `Owner` schema, so the code generator emits `getInitials`/`setInitials` on `OwnerDto`.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added an `@AfterMapping addInitials(...)` that sets `initials` to the upper-cased first letters of `firstName` and `lastName`, dot-separated with a trailing dot (e.g. `john`/`smith` → `J.S.`).

The new `AcceptanceTest.coreComputesInitials` passes and the full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The new `addInitials` method sits exactly where a maintainer of this codebase would expect it: as a sibling `@AfterMapping` default method immediately after the existing `addDisplayName`, following the identical pattern for derived, presentation-only fields on `OwnerDto`. It reuses the same javadoc style ("Fills the presentation-only {@code ...}"), the same `(Owner owner, @MappingTarget OwnerDto ownerDto)` signature, and lives in the right unit (the MapStruct mapper that already owns this DTO-shaping concern). No duplication, and the mapper isn't turning into a catch-all — it's the correct home for computed DTO fields. The `openapi.yml` addition likewise mirrors the adjacent `displayName` property (title/description/example/`readOnly: true`), keeping the schema consistent.
